utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: There's a disturbance --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: After that technical difficulty, I'll ask the Registrar to call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good afternoon. This is case number IT-99-37-I, the Prosecutor versus Slobodan Milosevic, Milan Milutinovic, Nikola Sainovic, Dragoljub Ojdanic, Vlajko Stojiljkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And may I have the appearances.

utterances.speaker: MS. DEL PONTE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The Prosecution is represented by myself, Prosecutor Carla Del Ponte, with my collaborator, Trial Attorney Christina Romano, and the Case Manager, Rebecca Graham.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Prosecutor. For the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, for the Defence, myself, Tomislav Visnjic, attorney-at-law from Belgrade, together with my colleagues Vojislav Selezan, an attorney-at-law from Belgrade, and Peter Robinson, an attorney-at-law from the United States of America.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This is the initial appearance of Mr. Ojdanic, and the initial appearance is conducted under Rule 62 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. At this hearing, the accused will be asked to enter a plea to the Second Amended Indictment in the case against him. Mr. Visnjic, may I take it that your client has received a copy of the indictment in a language that he understands and that you have had the opportunity of going through the indictment with him?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Does your client wish to have the indictment read out in full or is he prepared to waive that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, our client is prepared to waive his right to have the indictment read out to him in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. In that case, let the accused stand. Mr. Ojdanic, please stand. You have heard what your counsel has said. The indictment has been explained to you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I confirm what my lawyer said, that I have been familiarised with the contents of the indictment. I have understood it well, and I personally consider that there is no need for me to hear it once again here in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Ojdanic. Now, I'm going to read to you the counts in the Second Amended Indictment, and to each count you will enter a plea. Confine your answers to either "guilty" or "not guilty." Count 1 charges you with deportation, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(d) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. plead; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Count 2 charges you with other inhumane acts (forcible transfer), a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(i) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Counts 3 and 4 relate to the alleged killing of hundreds of Kosovo Albanian civilians between 1 January 1999 and 20 June 1999. Count 3 charges you with murder, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(a) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Also I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And count 4 charges you with murder, a violation of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal and recognised by Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions. How do you plead; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Count 5 charges you with persecutions on political, racial, and religious grounds, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(h) of the Statute. How do you plead; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. That completes the pleas. You may sit.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: There are two or three other matters incidental that I would raise at this time. Madam Prosecutor, I just remind you of the duty of the Prosecutor to make available to the Defence, in a language that the accused understands, within 30 days of the Initial Appearance, copies of all the supporting material which accompany the indictment, as well as all prior statements. That's the standard requirement under Rule 66(A)(i), and I take it that that obligation will be discharged. I come next to the question of the next hearing, a Status Conference. My intention is that this Status Conference should be organised as quickly as possible, because I foresee a number of incidental matters arising, both for the Defence as well as the Prosecutor. As you know, we have a very crowded timetable, and I would have liked to have had it organised to take place within a month. That has not proved to be possible, and the first date that's available is Friday, the 21st of June, at 3 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MS. DEL PONTE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I can inform the Court about the disclosure timetable. We have the total quantity of the material in English and in B/C/S, and that are, in total, 14 binders. For all except one of the binders, we have all material ready in English and B/C/S, and in relation to this binder, there are 30 pages still in translation process to B/C/S. So that we think that the translations can be completed and all binders ready for disclosure by Friday, 10 May. However, Your Honour, before we disclose the material fully, we will be filing a motion for non-disclosure of the material to the public. We will also be filing a motion to extend the protective measures applied to the Milosevic case to a certain witness to this case, and we would appreciate if we can wait to the response to the motion before disclosing the material. In any case, we are ready to start disclosure by Monday, 6 May. About the Status Conference, I take notice. We will be ready, and we will get in touch with the Defence counsel for this Status Conference preparation. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We will await the motions that you will file. Mr. Visnjic, anything that you wish to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not for the time being. Not until we receive some material from the Office of the Prosecutor. For the time being, there is nothing I have to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, there being no other matters, this hearing stands adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: at 2.45 p.m.
